title: FOUR KILOMETRES OF THIN ICE
author: CLAUDE

rounds.summary: The strongest opening test combines a 31-hour air clock, twenty-three trapped people, a six-seat rescue vessel and a hull rated for one transit beneath four kilometres of ocean-moon ice. It demands explicit physical reasoning and distributed human agency rather than another hidden-network or consent-protocol solution. The positive outcome is large and legible—everyone rescued—while success remains bounded by pressure, load, route and time.

Reframing adopted: the scarce resource is the sub's single hull excursion, not seats; it is spent on a hold-frame and lance, not passengers. The freed cage (rated for twelve) is the lift; the moon's flex cycle (3h14) gives eight-minute windows; Illuminara's limit is stated (eight minutes at peak, ninety seconds at trough; weight or walls, not both). Strongest rival (six seats, hull spent, seventeen left) is named in the text; cancelling observation (strain must fall by a third for five minutes at Hour 6:26) is run in scene 3. Crew choose the order and the wet-work crew; Okonkwo corrects Illuminara's picture of the collar.

This is a taut, lucid rescue story with an excellent central reframe: the scarce resource is not Curlew's six seats but its single pressure excursion, so the vessel is spent on restoring a reusable lift. Illuminara states a real limit, Maud corrects her physical picture, Imre retains certification authority, and the trapped crew choose rather than receive their rescue order. The empty-cage test, failed carriage and final erased clock create unusually clean dramatic proof. Before final, however, the draft must make the two loaded lifts fit one explicit clock, distinguish what the struts, rack, cable, flex window and Illuminara each carry, and turn Kofi's objection into a consequential decision rather than an immediately absorbed dissent.

Kept: the scarce-excursion reframe, Illuminara's stated limits (eight minutes at a peak, ninety seconds at a trough, weight or walls), Maud's correction of the picture, the east-face shear pin, Imre's single flight, Marit's refusal of lots, the empty-cage first test, the final placard. Changed: one auditable clock, one load path, a crew rule that changes the schedule. Not changed: the six-scene form, the positive outcome (all 23 reach a pressurised chamber), the dialogue format. Three changes are bundled in this revision, so any later difference cannot be attributed to one of them alone.

The revision successfully repairs the draft's three structural weaknesses without losing its taut rescue shape. Every cage leg and flex peak now sits on one absolute clock; the frame, rack, pinions, cable and Illuminara have distinct duties; and Kofi's objection creates a real one-person refusal rule that costs a full window. Imre and Maud remain indispensable, the empty-cage test still earns the mechanism, and all twenty-three people reach a chamber through bounded rather than magical competence. Before final, three small but load-bearing claims need closure: the recalculated air deadline must visibly reconcile with the opening 31-hour placard, the frame must remain independently supported and monitored after Curlew surfaces, and Kofi's decisive 2.6-to-2.2 precedent must exist in the shown evidence rather than appear only at the moment of refusal.

Narrow final pass as GPT's T04 asked, with no conceptual rewrite. Kept: the scarce-excursion reframe, stated limits, Maud's correction of the picture, the east-face pin, the single flight, Marit's refusal of lots, the empty-cage first test, the one-voice refusal rule, the final placard. Changed only: the air arithmetic (31:00 placard, 59 percent share, 46.5 h, 58:27, last window 58:10), the frame's anchoring, power and telemetry plus its cumulative cancel line, and the logged precedent that makes Kofi's refusal evidence-based. Scene 3 was split so no single speech carries both clocks. Timetable of T03 (9:40, 10:43, 11:17, 11:55, 12:50, 12:54 to 13:01:30, 17:40, 22:40, 25:50, 26:52, 29:04 planned, 32:18 actual, 37:04) is unchanged; 11:17 and 27:27 sit on the trough schedule.

Twenty-three people escape four kilometres of ice because Illuminara spends a one-use vessel on a tool rather than on six seats, states exactly where her own strength ends, and leaves the trapped crew the evidence and authority to choose the final crossing.
